Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Please state
your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim file for that.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in a parking lot in Pasadena, Texas, near the entrance of a grocery store. I'd just found a spot and was
backing out slowly.
Q: What happened next?
A: Another vehicle came down the aisle fairly fast. I didn't see it until it was almost on me. It clipped the rear corner of
my car. I hit my brakes, but the jolt still threw me forward and back.
Q: Did you have any contact with the other driver?
A: Briefly. They got out, said they were sorry, and asked if I was okay. We exchanged insurance information and that
was about it.
Q: When did you first notice you were hurt?
A: Not right away. By that evening my neck was stiff, and by the next morning I had pain running into my shouldres
and headaches.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since then?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the following day and then started physical therapy. The doctor said it looked like
whiplash.
Q: Are you still having symptoms?
A: Yes, I still have stiffness when I turn my head, and I've had trouble sleeping because of the neck pain.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Just that I'm willing to provide my medical records. I want this handled properly.
Q: Understood. Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
